findings.issue: Step 3 `/start` private branch checks `bot.getStatus() == CONNECTED` after the bot has already been resolved via `botRepository.findByProjectIdAndStatus(projectId, CONNECTED)` (line 49). The status predicate is therefore tautologically true at that point and the redundant check on line 50 is dead.
findings.fix: Drop the redundant `bot.getStatus() == CONNECTED` from the populate predicate at line 50 — the finder already guarantees CONNECTED. The atomic `findAndModify` Query on line 50 already independently includes `status=CONNECTED`, which is the only place the check actually matters.

findings.issue: AC line 108 reads `All four controller-owned counters register exactly: received (success), duration (Timer), rejected{invalid_secret}, rejected{project_not_found}, rejected{duplicate}.` That sentence promises four counters but enumerates five items; the Timer is not a counter (the title and Description both correctly say `4 counters + 1 Timer`).
findings.fix: Reword the AC to `All four controller-owned counters + one Timer register exactly: received (success counter), duration (Timer), rejected{invalid_secret} (counter), rejected{project_not_found} (counter), rejected{duplicate} (counter).` so the noun count matches the enumeration.

findings.issue: Context Files line 116 lists `AC17` (ownerChatId set) as relevant user-spec for this controller task, but the actual ownerChatId write is performed by the worker (T9). The controller only enqueues; AC17 verification belongs to ProcessTelegramUpdateJobTest. Including AC17 here can mislead the implementer into adding a controller-side test that the AC9 test cases cannot satisfy.
findings.fix: Remove `AC17` from the user-spec context-file reference line for T10 (and from any AC carry-forward implied here). AC17 is correctly owned by T9 (already listed there).
